Design settings

Shared interaction guidance

Every component follows these, and every component prompt repeats them.

  • int-01Hover, focus and press answer within the quick duration on the shared ease, and nothing waits for an animation to finish before it responds. Why: a control that answers at once feels solid, and one tempo across every component makes the product feel like one thing.
  • int-02Keyboard focus is always visible, moves in reading order, and stays where it was when something on the screen changes. Why: people who use a keyboard, switch or screen reader lose their place when focus disappears or jumps.
  • int-03A press is acknowledged by a change of colour, never by a change of size or position. Why: a control that grows or shifts moves its neighbours and the target under the pointer.
  • int-04Animate only what shows a change of state: something opening, arriving, lifting or finishing. Nothing loops for decoration or plays on page load. Why: motion that means something gets noticed; motion that does not is noise and slows people down.
  • int-05A control that is busy or has just acted keeps its place and its height, and says in words what is happening ("Saving", "Copied"). Why: the layout stays still, and the result is clear without relying on a spinner or a colour alone.
  • int-06When the system asks for reduced motion, every transition is instant and nothing moves; no meaning depends on motion. Why: motion makes some people dizzy or sick, and the interface must be fully understandable without it.
